findings.message: The broken-gate rows assert only `False-alarm rate:** UNKNOWN` and a non-zero exit. The fix was applied at two call sites, the vulnerable-sample catch path and the fixed-sample false-alarm path, but only the fixed-sample site is proved. If the `|| ! h="$(headings "$r")"` guard is removed from the vulnerable-sample site, both rows stay green: the fixed-sample site alone still gives UNKNOWN and a non-zero exit. Add an assertion that the catch rate is also UNKNOWN, e.g. `grep -q "Catch rate:\*\* UNKNOWN"` and `! grep -q "Catch rate:\*\* 0%"`, for each broken gate.
findings.scenario: Remove the gate-status guard from the vulnerable-sample branch (`if [ -z "$r" ]; then`), then run with SPECCLAW_INFOSEC_GATE=$TMP/bin/crashing-gate. The gate crash is read as no heading, so v_answered is incremented and the run reports `Catch rate:** 0%` instead of UNKNOWN. The new test still passes because it checks only the false-alarm line and the exit code, so the class fix at the second call site is unproven.
